title: fix(post): G82/G89 dwell reopens the cycle on Fanuc, Mazak, Doosan, grblHAL and Tormach
body:
## What changed

The pattern of PR #2355 (Haas) goes into five more posts. The dwell is part of the cycle signature. A changed dwell writes G80 and a new cycle block with its own P. A hole with the same dwell keeps the modal short form (bare X Y).

- `assets/posts/fanuc.cps`, `assets/posts/mazak.cps`, `assets/posts/doosan-dnm.cps`: the signature of G82 and G89 includes the dwell in ms.
- `assets/posts/grblhal.cps`, `assets/posts/tormach.cps`: the signature of G82, G86 and G89 includes the dwell in seconds. These two posts also write a G86 P, so G86 has the same defect.
- All five posts: a back-bore with a dwell of 0 posts G85 (feed in, feed out), not G89 with no P. A drill with a dwell of 0 posts G81, as before. Thus a dwell of 0 writes no P word, and no old P stays active.

The PR #2351 G83 dwell refusal and the PR #2048 behaviour do not change.

## Readings

- Fanuc G82/G89 formats give P as the dwell; G85 has no P. No public source that we read confirms `P0` on Fanuc, Mazak or Doosan. Thus G85 is used for a zero-dwell back-bore. G85 is the same motion as G89 with no dwell.
- LinuxCNC G-code reference: G82, G86 and G89 take P in seconds, G85 has no P. The LinuxCNC interpreter (`interp_cycles.cc`, `convert_cycle_xy`) keeps the last P (`cycle_p`) for a block without P in the same motion mode. It refuses a G82, G86 or G89 block without P after G80.
- The decision is in `docs/decisions/2360-dwell-cycle-signature.md`.

## Pinning tests

`crates/post/tests/dwell_cycles_modal_p.rs` (5 tests, each over the five posts; the G86 test over grblHAL and Tormach):

- `g82_rewrites_p_when_the_dwell_changes`
- `g82_then_g89_each_hole_posts_its_own_p`
- `dwell_to_zero_leaves_no_p_active`
- `same_dwell_keeps_the_open_group` (guard: the short form stays)
- `linuxcnc_family_g86_rewrites_p_when_the_dwell_changes`

On the post files of `origin/main`, 4 of the 5 tests fail. `same_dwell_keeps_the_open_group` passes on both, as it must.

## Gate

- `cargo test -p camcraft-post`: 80 test binaries, 674 tests passed, 0 failed.
- `cargo test -p camcraft-app --test conformance`: 7 passed. No golden `.nc` changed.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-post --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.

## Not exercised

- No real Fanuc, Mazak, Doosan, grblHAL or PathPilot control ran the output.
- The other `camcraft-app` post suites did not run. No golden changed.
- A zero-dwell G86 on grblHAL and Tormach still posts with no P. The LinuxCNC interpreter refuses it after G80. That is filed as #2362 (`P3`) and is not in this PR.

Changelog: Fanuc, Mazak, Doosan, grblHAL and Tormach posts write each hole's own dwell P on G82 and G89 (and G86 on grblHAL and Tormach); a back-bore with no dwell posts G85.

Effort: high

Fixes #2360

title: fix(post): Haas G82 and G89 post each hole's own dwell P
body:
## What changed

`assets/posts/haas.cps`, `onCycle`: the open-cycle signature was `g|Z|R|Q` for G82 and G89. When two holes in one open group had different dwells, the second hole was posted as a bare `X Y` block and ran the first hole's modal P. That is wrong posted G-code (P1).

- The dwell is now part of the signature for G82, G83 and G89. #2048 already did this for G83, and the code now covers the three dwell cycles together. When the dwell changes, the post writes `G80` and issues the cycle again with the new hole's own P.
- G89 now always writes P, and writes `P0` for a zero dwell. Without it, a reissued G89 would pick up the old modal P (Haas G04/G83 documentation: P is modal). G82 is chosen only for a positive dwell (a zero-dwell drill posts G81), so G82 always carries its P already.
- Holes with the same dwell stay in the open group as bare `X Y` blocks, as before.

Haas output changes only when G82/G89 holes in one group have different dwells, or for a zero-dwell G89, which gains `P0`. No existing golden changes: `synth_haas.nc` has one G82 that already writes `P500`, and no G89.

The change stays inside the Haas post. It follows #2048's G83 approach: dwell in the signature, P0 clears the modal dwell. It does not touch the files of #2351 (grblHAL/Tormach) or the Sinumerik post (#2349).

Decision: `docs/decisions/2350-haas-g82-g89-dwell.md`.

## How tested

New pin `crates/post/tests/haas_dwell_cycles.rs`:
- `haas_g82_rewrites_p_when_the_dwell_changes`: two G82 holes, 0.5 s then 0.75 s, give P500 then P750.
- `haas_g89_rewrites_p_when_the_dwell_changes`: the same for G89.
- `haas_g89_zero_dwell_writes_p0`: G89 with 0.5 s then 0 s gives P500 then P0; a single zero-dwell G89 gives P0.
- `haas_same_dwell_keeps_the_open_group`: with an unchanged dwell, the second hole is still a bare X Y block.

On the old `haas.cps`, the first three fail (the second hole had no P, `[Some("P500"), None]`). With the fix all four pass.

Quick gate `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main`: green, 66 steps, 0 failed (includes post suites haas_dwell_cycles, g83_dwell, script_haas and the app post suites). `cargo clippy -p camcraft-post --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.

## Not exercised

No real Haas control was run. Haas's G85 still writes a positive P, which this PR leaves alone (out of scope, #1445).

Changelog: Haas post: G82 and G89 holes in one cycle group now each post their own dwell P (a changed dwell reissues the cycle; a zero-dwell G89 writes P0) instead of running the previous hole's modal dwell (#2350)

title: feat(post): wrapped A on the Tormach microARC 4 (G93, cumulative A)
body:
## What changed

`assets/posts/tormach.cps` no longer refuses an A that changes inside an operation on an A-about-X machine. It now posts it as wrapped (simultaneous) A, based on mkinney's four PathPilot Hub readings on #796 (v2.14.4, 770MX SIM, 4th axis on):

- **A is cumulative.** PathPilot treats A as plain degrees with no rollover (A350 -> `G1 A10` turned back 340 deg). Each target is the nearest equivalent of the held angle: 179 -> 181, 359 -> 361, never back through 0. A count past the stated travel is refused by name.
- **A turning X Y Z feed is G93.** `F = 1 / t`, where t (min) = max((the tip's path relative to the part + one rounding step) / the programmed feed, the posted |dA| / the stated A rate). F is floored to 0.001, so rounding only ever slows a move. Neither the cutting feed nor the A rate is exceeded. The rate comes from `rotaryRate` (#885).
- **An A-only feed stays G94**, with F in deg/min under the same time law (Hub reading 4). Feeds that don't turn A are unchanged. G94 is restated before any motion that is not a G93 feed and at every section end.
- **Turning moves are split onto their segment.** The machine moves XYZ in a line while A turns, so the tip relative to the part bows off the stream's segment. Each turning move (rapids too) is split into 2^k pieces until the bow is within 0.005 mm (at most 256 pieces, else refused by name).
- **A is reset between operations:** as before (#785), each section restates its first A as -180..180 after `G53 G0 Z0`, so a wrap that ended at A300 unwinds at the top of Z.
- **Refused by name:** a machine file with no A rate ("states no A feed rate"), a count past the travel ("A counts on through 360 (PathPilot does not roll A over)"), an arc / canned cycle / probe move that would turn A, a turning move from an unknown start, and a move that still bows after 256 splits.
- `assets/machines/tormach-770mx-microarc4.mch` now states A `max_normal_speed` 360 deg/min. That is the rate the Hub ran as asked. It is conservative: no Tormach rate could be cited with confidence.
- Docs: the tester-kit README, `first-4axis-part.md` and `continuous-4-axis.md` (with its site test), plus `docs/decisions/796-tormach-wrapped-a.md`. The kit's `.camproj` was re-saved by its own test, so it carries the A rate.

Fork branch based on upstream `main` at 4e8616b (not a cut tag), so the #885 rule and the current post are in.

## How tested

New pins in `crates/app/tests/tormach_wrapped_a.rs` (10 tests):
- `a_long_xyz_move_takes_its_time_from_the_feed`: `G93 G1 X50 Y0 Z0 A1 F11.999` (50 mm at F600)
- `a_mostly_rotary_move_takes_its_time_from_the_a_rate`: `G1 X51 Y0 Z0 A91 F4` (90 deg at 360 deg/min)
- `g94_comes_back_before_an_xyz_only_feed_and_a_turns_in_deg_per_min`
- `a_counts_on_through_180_and_360_never_back_through_0`
- `the_next_operation_resets_a_at_the_safe_z`
- `a_section_that_ends_in_g93_restates_g94_before_m5`
- `a_turning_move_off_the_axis_is_split_onto_its_chord`: every posted point, turned back into the part, lies on the stream's chord, and each piece is held to both rates
- `a_count_past_the_travel_is_refused_by_name`, `a_machine_with_no_a_rate_is_refused_by_name`, `the_microarc_states_its_a_rate`

Golden: `crates/app/tests/golden/nc/tormach/wrap_rotary_parallel_microarc4.nc` is the microARC kit's job plus a real Rotary Parallel (1/8" ball) on the bar. It is pinned by `microarc_test_part::a_wrapped_op_on_the_test_part_posts_wrapped_a`, which replaces `a_wrapped_op_on_the_test_part_is_refused_by_name` and also checks A unwrapping, G93 on every turning XYZ feed, G94 elsewhere, and G94 at the section end.

Updated: `tormach_fourth_axis::an_a_that_changes_inside_an_operation_posts_wrapped_a` (was `..._is_refused`). In `fourth_axis_pose`, the two fanuc tests on the microARC file now place A with a rapid first, because that file now states an A rate and the #885 rule asks for it. The recorded `rotary.refusal` golden for tormach (tilt-head machine) now names the B tilt refusal instead.

Gate (macOS, debug, targeted - `cargo xtask gate quick` plans every app suite because a new golden is shared test input, so the touched suites ran instead): every camcraft-app test binary that names Tormach / the microARC (69 binaries, incl. `tormach_wrapped_a`, `microarc_test_part`, `tormach_fourth_axis`, `fourth_axis_pose`, `first_4axis_part`, `index_swing`, `tormach_post`, `rotary_feed_cap`, `recorded_post_streams`) and every camcraft-post binary that names Tormach or the recorded streams (45 binaries, incl. `script_tormach`, `explain_tormach`, `recorded_streams`): all green. `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app` on the four changed test files `-D warnings`: clean. `site/tests/test_first_4axis_part.py`: the updated tests pass; `test_machine_and_post_are_the_shipped_ones` fails the same way on upstream main (machine name not in `posting.rs`), not touched here.

## Not exercised

- No real cut, and this exact program has not been run in the Hub. The readings cover single test moves only.
- PathPilot's A soft limits. The file keeps -360..360, and a wrap past it is refused.

## Hub check (before trusting it on the 770MX + microARC 4)

Run slowly (feed override 25-50 %, single block for the first lines), with the tool lifted 1" above the work offset (air cut):
1. Post the golden's WRAP op (or `wrap_rotary_parallel_microarc4.nc`) and load it in the Hub 770MX SIM with the 4th axis on. Confirm it loads with no error on `G93` / `G94` lines and no "F word missing".
2. Watch the A DRO on a stretch that passes 180 (e.g. line 1393 of the golden, A180 -> A185.757): A must keep counting up, never swing back through 0.
3. Time one long G93 line against its F (time = 1/F min). Check one A-only `G1 A.. F360` runs at 6 deg/s.
4. Confirm the control is back in G94 after the WRAP op (Status tab / the next op's feeds run at their ipm).
5. Check PathPilot's A soft limits (jog A past +360 / -360 in the SIM) and report them on #796, so the machine file's travel can be stated.
6. Only then air-cut on the real machine at a low override, the bar in the chuck, a hand on feed hold.

Changelog: Tormach PathPilot post: continuous (wrapped) A on the microARC 4 - A counts on past 360, turning feeds in G93 held to the feed and the stated A rate (360 deg/min); refused by name when the machine states no A rate or the count passes the A travel (#796)

Fixes #796

body:
Stacked on #2162 (merge #2162 first)

## What changed
- Added the clean-room Mach4 milling postprocessor in `assets/posts/mach4.cps`.
- Left 3-axis programs in `G94` mode with `G20`/`G21` unit blocks, `G90 G94 G91.1 G40 G49 G17 G64` safety header, `G17`/`G18`/`G19` arcs, `G41`/`G42`/`G40` cutter compensation, `G54`..`G59` and `G54.1 P1`..`P248` work offsets, `G28`/`G53`/`G30` safe retracts, `G73`/`G81`/`G82`/`G83`/`G84`/`G85`/`G86`/`G89` canned cycles with decimal-second `P` dwells, and `G31` Macro B probing.
- Added 3+2 indexed AC trunnion support in `G94` (no `G43.4` or `G93`) using `#1962`'s trunnion schema (`A` parent of `C`, `pivot`, `offset`, `zeroOffset`, `rollover`, `signConvention`, `controller.rtcp = false`).
- Added analytical AC inverse kinematics, platter-center G54 datum transform (`work_datum = a_pivot + c_offset`), rotated cardinal arc projection, optional paired `rotaryUnclamp`/`rotaryClamp` M-codes, and safe-retract-only `C` rollover handling (`rollover_360` vs `unwrapped`).
- Added named refusals when `controller.rtcp` is `true`, when AC trunnion geometry or travel bounds are invalid or missing, or when an indexed section changes tool orientation during cutting (`"needs #1966: inverse-time feed"`).
- Registered `"Mach4"` in `BUILTINS` in `crates/app/src/posting.rs` and added `"Mach4"` conformance and script entries in `crates/app/tests/conformance.rs` and `crates/post/tests/script_mach4.rs`.
- Documented unattended choices in `docs/decisions/1968-mach4-post.md`.

## Cause
Camcraft shipped no Mach4 milling dialect, and Mach4 controllers lack native Fanuc `G43.4` RTCP while `#1966` (`G93` inverse-time feed) is not yet merged.

  - When the first operation has no toolpath, the playback shows the uncut stock of that operation's setup.
- A separate line under the transport bar names the stop: "Stock simulation stops before 2D Contour1: it has no toolpath. Generate it to see the rest." title: fix(3d): prevent shared-depth XY crossings in adaptive microlifts, helices, and offset shells
body:
## What changed

- Landed `entry::helix_about`'s final half-turn on exact `z1` and clamped intermediate `lattice` depths monotonically toward `z1` ([entry.rs](crates/motion/src/entry.rs)).
- Extracted shared depth-overlap and `CROSSING_TOUCH = 1e-9` segment-crossing checks (`z_depths_overlap`, `proper_cross_touch`, `seg_crosses_prior`, `moves_cross_prior`) in `machining2d::arc_cross` and re-exported them internally ([arc_cross.rs](crates/motion/src/machining2d/arc_cross.rs), [mod.rs](crates/motion/src/machining2d/mod.rs)).
- Scaled `microlift::link_at` lift heights strictly below the nearest earlier horizontal `Feed` cut plane above `z`, probed candidate links against prior `Feed` moves, promoted crossing low links to `high: true` down-only links when clear, and fell back to a `hop_z` rapid plus `Plunge` retract when even `down` crosses or the gap is `<= 0.02 mm` ([microlift.rs](crates/motion/src/machining2d/microlift.rs)).
- Protected 3-D offset shells by probing `descent::push_helix` against posted `b.moves()` (re-placing around `along_pass`/`dive_room` or calling `fallback` when no bore clears) and hopping over any `level_ctx::feed_leg` chord that crosses a prior `Feed` move at shared depth or Z band ([descent.rs](crates/motion/src/machining3d/descent.rs), [level_ctx.rs](crates/motion/src/machining3d/level_ctx.rs)).
- Added unit and integration pinning tests ([entry.rs](crates/motion/src/entry.rs), [microlift.rs](crates/motion/src/machining2d/microlift.rs), [pocket3d_mask_edge.rs](crates/motion/tests/pocket3d_mask_edge.rs)) and recorded the unattended design choices ([2237-pocket3d-mask-crossing.md](docs/decisions/2237-pocket3d-mask-crossing.md)).

- `microlift::link_at` applied `0.30..1.50 mm` lifts without checking the stepdown gap above `z` or whether candidate microlifts crossed same-level entry ramps/helices.
- `descent::bore_meets_lifted_leg` only checked `lvl.passes` at `pz`, missing lifted moves emitted by earlier levels into `b.moves()`.
- `level_ctx::feed_leg` emitted shifted `OffsetRings + shell` floor passes at `bottom_z` across `x/y` already cut by the penultimate level's `floor_z`-clamped pass at exact `bottom_z`.

title: fix(ui): show a progress overlay over the viewport while a toolpath generates
body: #2257: while an operation generates its toolpath, the viewport shows no progress. The cause is that generation ran in the frame, on the UI thread. Thus no frame painted until the job ended. ## What changed - **Generation on a worker** (native window only). `GenerateOperation` already had a seam between the world reads and the pure work (M5.3 B). That seam is now public as `StagedGeneration`: - `StagedGeneration::new` reads the world on the UI thread. - `StagedGeneration::finish` runs the generator, the verification and the stamp on a worker thread. - The result lands through the same undoable `GenerateOperation` as before. The generators, the verify check and the post gate do not change. - **The overlay** (`crates/ui/src/egui_app/gen_overlay.rs`) lies at the top centre of the viewport while a job runs. The navigation strip at the bottom and the view cube stay clear. It shows: - the label of the operation; - "(2 of 5)" when more generations wait in the queue; - the elapsed time and an activity bar (the generators report no fraction); - a `Cancel generation` button. - **Stale results are discarded.** The user can edit, undo or delete while the worker runs. A result lands only while its operation and its cached path are the same as at staging (`GenerateOperation::still_current`). If not, the status line says: `generation of X discarded: the operation changed while it generated - generate it again`. - **Cancel** drops the result and the queue. The old toolpath stays. A worker that runs finishes in the background, and its result is ignored. - **New and Open** drop a running generation. A result for the old document never lands in the new one. - **The viewport takes no press inside the overlay.** A click on Cancel is not also a viewport pick. - **Only the window turns it on** (`State::gen_jobs.background`). Tests, headless runs, scripts and MCP keep the synchronous path. `State::settle` waits for the worker. The browser has no threads: a failed spawn runs the job in place, as the import worker does. - **Repaint:** the shell asks for a repaint every 50 ms only while a job runs or waits (`view_pass::state_redraw_delay`). A frame with no job does no more work than before (#2238). - **No world search in a frame.** The job finds its operation entity one time, when it starts. Each frame reads the label from that entity (`model::live_operation_label`, which checks that the entity is alive). A rename shows at once. A deleted operation shows its name. - Decision record: `docs/decisions/2257-generate-progress-overlay.md`. ## What it looks like Rendered headless from the seeded shell at 1280x800 (a throwaway test, not in the branch). The images are below. - Before: while `Contour1` generates, the viewport shows nothing. - After: the overlay at the top centre, with the operation name, the elapsed time, the activity bar and `Cancel generation`. **Before** (the viewport while `Contour1` generates): **After** (the overlay at the top centre): ## Tests New pinning tests: - `crates/ui/src/egui_app/tests/generate_progress.rs` (structural; the result comes through a channel that the test holds, so no frame races a real generator): - `the_overlay_names_the_running_operation_and_goes_when_it_lands`: the overlay text `Generating Contour1 - ...` is over the viewport, and the Cancel button is there while the job runs. The status says that the generation is cancelled. A rename shows in the overlay with no new search. - `a_deleted_operation_shows_its_name_and_no_dead_entity_is_read`: the overlay shows `Contour1` after a delete. Without the `is_alive` check, the test process stops (0xc0000409). - `crates/app/tests/generate_staged.rs`: - `staged_then_finished_lands_what_the_one_shot_command_lands`: the same path either way. - `a_result_is_stale_after_an_edit_a_generation_or_a_delete` Gates on 08022981: - `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main` (222 steps): green, with two exceptions. title: fix(2d): hold crossing law on OffsetRings and Waterline pockets
body:
## What changed
- Updated `emit_pocket_passes` in `crates/motion/src/machining2d/pocket_emit.rs` to hold `post_crossing_free` whenever `hold_crossings` is set or the strategy fits pass arcs (`Adaptive`, `OffsetRings`, or `Waterline`).
- Counted fitted arcs into `proof.arcs` in the `fit_arcs` branch so `ProofTally::note()` reports accurate totals when a crossing arc returns to chords.
- Added unit pin `offset_rings_across_one_micron_vertex_step_post_crossing_free` and integration suite `crates/app/tests/adaptive_fig8_crossing.rs`.
- Recorded the design decision in `docs/decisions/2240-adaptive-fig8-crossing.md`.

## Cause
- On `fig8.step` (tight stock or stock excluding the top face), 2D Adaptive refuses the HSM planner and falls back to `PocketStrategy::OffsetRings`.
- Clipper2 integer quantization (`1e-6 mm` grid) on STEP-faceted circles creates micron-scale vertex steps that split `fit_arcs` across `sag_bound` into `[Arc, 1 um Line, Arc]`.

The before renders reproduce the prior behavior with temporary reversions: disable history-group folding for undo; restore the former Native confirmation allowlist and bypass the newly added live gate for `load_machine` for machine loading. The after renders use the current PR behavior. All capture edits were restored; no screenshots or capture code were added to this PR branch.

Existing pins were mutation-checked again: `one_ctrl_z_reverts_multi_call_ai_chat_turn` and `machine_and_limit_edits_require_confirmation_and_unapproved_live_dispatch_blocks` both failed with their behavior reverted and passed after restoration.

## What changed
- Added `BatchCommand` and stackable `History::begin_group` / `commit_group` / `cancel_group` in `crates/app/src/commands/batch.rs` and `crates/app/src/commands/mod.rs`.
- Wired `State::submit_ai_prompt`, `State::run`, `AiChatState::poll`, and `ChatTurn::finish` so a contiguous multi-call AI turn commits as one `BatchCommand` undo step (`Ctrl+Z` / `Ctrl+Y`).
- Added the read-only `get_selection` MCP tool (`crates/app/src/mcp/selection.rs`) and `SelectionContext` snapshot (`State::selection_context`) so live sessions report selected entities, active setup, selected/active operation, viewport `pick_mode`, and `geometry_picks` without breaking `ui -> app` layering.
- Added `LiveGate`, `GateKind`, `ApprovedCall`, `requires_approval`, `LiveOptions`, and `answer_live_with` in `crates/app/src/mcp/live.rs`; `answer_live` now fails closed via `&LiveOptions::default()`.
- Updated `AiChatState`, `transport::requires_confirmation`, `worker`, and `mcp_host::pump` to share `requires_approval` and `is_read_only_tool`, bind `Allow` clicks to one `ApprovedCall`, and never auto-approve `post`, `load_machine`, or `edit_machine`.

- Recorded design decisions in `docs/decisions/1942-ai-chat-safety.md`.

## Cause
Before this fix, AI chat turns pushed one `History` entry per tool call (requiring multiple `Ctrl+Z` presses), `get_selection` did not exist for AI inspection of viewport picks, `FallbackMode::Native` skipped confirmation for machine and limit tools, and `answer_live` lacked a server-side permission gate.

## Tests
Pinning tests (all red on unchanged `upstream/main` `e808c9629`, green after fix):
- `camcraft-app --test batch_undo`: `begin_and_commit_group_folds_multi_command_turn_into_one_undo_step`, `empty_and_nested_groups_and_direct_batch_command_behave_cleanly`, `cancel_group_keeps_existing_commands_separate` (3 passed, 0 failed).

title: fix(3d): keep masked 3D Pocket clear to open edges
body:
## What changed
- Extracted `mask_center` in `crates/motion/src/machining3d/ladder.rs` and added `MASK_RESIDUE = 1.0`.
- `ladder` now erodes the unmasked `target` by `r + stock_to_leave` first so only model islands act as walls.
- `mask_center` intersects `mask.above(z)` with `center.offset(r)` (the swept envelope of `center`) instead of raw `target`.
- `mask_center` opens the standing region by `MASK_RESIDUE * mask.cell()` using mitered offsets (`offset_sharp`) to drop one-cell lattice residue on walls without rounding grid corners.
- `mask_center` then intersects `center` with `standing.offset(r)` so only centers whose disc meets standing stock remain.
- Added `masked_empty` tracking in `ladder` so levels emptied by the mask report nothing left to cut instead of "too narrow".
- Added `crates/motion/tests/pocket3d_mask_edge.rs` and `docs/decisions/1749-mask-edge.md`.

## Cause
In `sc_logo.camproj`, `S1 Adaptive rough profile` cleared the stock just outside the part silhouette before `S1 Notch adaptive + terrace finish` ran. Because `ladder` intersected `target` with the mask before eroding by the tool radius, the mask boundary acted as a wall one radius thick and left standing stock at the notch open edges where Setup 2 `Soft jaw (9)` stands. title: fix(post): apply stored script options for named posts and warn on mismatch
body:
## What changed

- Added `posting::resolve_cps` to return both the resolved `PostRef` and script text for a post name or `.cps` path. Kept `resolve_cps_text` as a thin wrapper.
- Added `posting::post_script_for_post_with_options` and `posting_mounts::post_mounts_for_post_with_options`. Threaded the optional `PostRef` through single-mount (`post_script_as`) and multi-mount (`post_each`) posting into `program_options_for_script`.
- Added `setup_post_options::same_post` and updated `setup_post_options::script_for_post`. `PostRef::Builtin` and `PostRef::Named` match via `post_key`, and `PostRef::File` entries fall back to canonical path matching via `std::fs::canonicalize`.
- Added `setup_post_options::unapplied_script_warning` and wired it into `script::api::v_post` (shared by MCP `post`, JS `cam.post`, and CLI `process --cps`).
- Added optional `"warning"` output to `script::report::posted_view`, `PostResult` docs in `script/mod.rs`, `assets/scripts/cam.d.ts`, and `env.logs` for CLI runs when stored `script_options` of the document or a setup's configured post did not apply.
- Recorded the design choice in `docs/decisions/2190-named-post-script-options.md`.

## Cause

`script::api::v_post` called `posting::resolve_cps_text`, which discarded the resolved `PostRef`. It then called `post_mounts_script_with_options`, which passed `post: None` into `post_script_as` and omitted `explicit_post` in `post_each`. Because `program_options_for_script` saw `post: None`, it skipped `setup_post_options::script_for_post` and silently dropped all stored `PostScriptOptions`. `script_for_post` also lacked canonical path fallback for `PostRef::File` keys, and nothing warned when an explicit post left configured `script_options` unapplied.

title: fix(post): split near-180 R arcs and verify chord <= 2|R| after rounding
body:
## What changed
- Updated `emitArcWithRadius` in `assets/posts/fanuc.cps`, `assets/posts/haas.cps`, `assets/posts/mazak.cps`, `assets/posts/doosan-dnm.cps`, `assets/posts/tormach.cps`, and `assets/posts/grblhal.cps`.
- The helper computes both endpoint radii `r0` and `r1`, uses the mean `r = (r0 + r1) * 0.5`, and falls back to I/J/K when `Math.abs(r0 - r1) > Math.min(0.02, Math.max(0.002, r * 0.005))`.
- The helper splits full and near-360 degree arcs (`full || sweep >= 2 * Math.PI - Math.PI / 9`) into 4 quadrant segments, splits near-180 degree arcs (`Math.abs(sweep - Math.PI) <= Math.PI / 9`) into 2 ~90 degree segments, and interpolates axis `h` linearly per segment.
- `buildSegs` checks every segment after output rounding (`fu(...)` relative to `[orgX, orgY, orgZ]`): `rp > 0`, `chord > 0`, `chord <= 2 * rp - 1e-7`, and `chord <= 2 * rp * 0.99` when unsplit (`count === 1`, re-splitting into quadrants if triggered).
- When any guard fails, `emitArcWithRadius` returns `false` before calling `block(...)`, so `onCircular` falls back cleanly to I/J/K without partial output or stale plane state.
- Added `crates/post/tests/radius_arcs.rs` to pin all six posts and recorded the trade-offs in `docs/decisions/2191-radius-arcs-180.md`.

## Cause
- `emitArcWithRadius` computed `R` only from `from -> center` and split only exact full circles (`< 1e-5`).
- Helix half-turns from the 1 micron lattice carry slight endpoint radius differences and 180 degree sweeps, so separate rounding of `X`/`Y`/`Z` (`wo(...)`) and `R` (`w("R", ...)`) wrote `R1.235`/`R1.234` and chords longer than `2|R|` (`2.469 > 2.468`), while magnifying center drift near 180 degrees.

## Tests
- Pins in `crates/post/tests/radius_arcs.rs` (across `fanuc`, `haas`, `mazak`, `doosan-dnm`, `tormach`, `grblhal`):
  - `helix_half_turns_use_reachable_r_and_stay_on_circle` (red before fix, green after)
  - `near_180_and_full_circle_arcs_in_all_planes_hold_chord_and_center` (red before fix, green after)
  - `inch_and_nonzero_origin_arcs_hold_after_rounding` (red before fix, green after)
  - `major_arcs_use_negative_r_and_degenerate_arcs_fall_back_to_ijk` (red before fix, green after)
  - `recorded_arc_streams_post_valid_r_arcs`
- Mutation checks on `assets/posts/fanuc.cps` (each guard reverted -> red, restored -> green):
  - Removing the radius-mismatch guard failed `major_arcs_use_negative_r_and_degenerate_arcs_fall_back_to_ijk` (`fanuc/mismatch`); restoring passed all 5 tests.
  - Disabling the near-180 / near-360 split and `0.99` chord guard (keeping the old 2-way full-circle split) failed 4 tests; restoring passed all 5 tests.
  - Removing the post-rounding `rp > 0` and `chord <= 2 * rp` checks failed `major_arcs_use_negative_r_and_degenerate_arcs_fall_back_to_ijk` (`fanuc/tiny_inch`); restoring passed all 5 tests.
- Checks after final edit:
  - `cargo test -p camcraft-post --test radius_arcs`: 5 passed, 0 failed.
  - `cargo clippy -p camcraft-post --all-targets -- -D warnings`: green (0 warnings).
  - `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings`: green (0 warnings).
- `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main`:
  - `[01] post suites` (42 suites): passed in 23s.

title: fix(multiaxis): refuse out-of-range 3+2 tilt by name and keep A0 B180 plane X on machine X

## What changed

- Added `Tilt::refusal` in `crates/app/src/operation/types/params.rs` and wired it into `OpParams::named_refusal` (`crates/app/src/operation/types/sane.rs`). - Updated `apply_hint` in `crates/ui/src/feedback.rs` to show `draft.named_refusal()` before the generic unusable-value text.
- Updated `TiltedFrame::new` in `crates/cl/src/cl/frame.rs` to zero out axis components smaller than `1e-12` when selecting the tie-breaking seed axis. The `A 0` / `B 180` frame now keeps plane X along machine `+X` (the A rotary axis).
- Updated `site/content/guide/getting-started/first-4axis-part.md`, `crates/app/tests/first_4axis_part.rs`, and `examples/first-4axis-part.camproj` so `Flat A180` uses the same `-0.75, 0` to `-0.25, 0` ends as the other three flats.
- Saved `Tilt.basis_version` with each tilted operation. A missing version uses basis 0 and preserves the original coordinates and digest. New UI and MCP drafts use basis 1 with a distinct cache stamp. The loader refuses an unknown basis version.
- Advanced the project format from version 62 to version 63. Older builds refuse these saved files instead of ignoring `basis_version` and rotating regenerated cuts.
- Recorded the design choices in `docs/decisions/2133-tilt-a180-refusal-basis.md`.

## Apply hint screenshots

These images render the shipping shell with egui_kittest. Both images show the same Face draft at A 180 and B 0.
The viewport uses the harness placeholder. The operation page and the Apply hint use the shipping widgets.

The after image uses `feedback.rs` from reviewed head `e955c9dfed47e7c2d1ce0a73ffd335fa72c04a99`.

1. `Tilt::is_sane` returned `bool` with no entry in `OpParams::named_refusal`. `CreateOperation`, `EditOperationParams`, MCP `add_operation`/`edit_operation`, and the UI Apply hint fell back to generic "not usable" text without stating the limits or the `A 0` / `B 180` pose.
2. `TiltedFrame::from_angles(origin, 0.0, 180.0)` produces `axis[0] = sin(180 deg) ~ 1.22e-16` while `axis[1] = 0.0`. `TiltedFrame::new` compared magnitudes without a float-dust threshold, picked the Y axis as seed instead of X, and swapped plane X and Y on the `A 0` / `B 180` face.

- **Compatibility pins (`tilt_basis_compat`):**
  - `old_project_keeps_basis_status_regeneration_and_posted_cut` checks an old project at load, status, regeneration, and posting.

title: feat(import): open Solidcraft .sc designs as a model
body:
Needs maintainer: adds the native camcraft-geometry -> camcraft-kernel dependency (decision file included).

Branch base: upstream/main af83da0f.

## What changed
- CamCraft opens a Solidcraft `.sc` design as a model. The app reads the cached final body of the design.
- Model > Open offers `.sc`. A viewport drop takes `.sc`. MCP `import_model` takes `.sc`.
- These three use the one model import. The `Format::Solidcraft` arm in app dispatches to the re-exported `camcraft_geometry::solidcraft` parser.
- The module calls `camcraft_kernel::solidcraft::import_solidcraft`. Then it meshes the body with `camcraft_kernel::machining_mesh::machining_mesh` at the STEP chord cap (0.005 mm).
- A damaged or unsupported `.sc` is refused by name. The message is "Solidcraft design refused: <kernel reason>". The model is not added and the history does not change.
- A watchdog requests cooperative cancellation after 300 seconds. The kernel planner has no cancellation hook. Completion within 300 seconds is not guaranteed.
- A STEP facet budget for a `.sc` is refused by name, as for STL and OBJ.
- The kernel edge is native only. The browser build does not offer `.sc`, and it refuses `.sc` by name.
- `camcraft-kernel` re-exports `CancelToken`, so geometry does not need its own solidcore dependency.
- Open and drop now use one extension list (`state::MODEL_EXTENSIONS`). The drop refusal message comes from that list.
- Decision file: `docs/decisions/1456-sc-open.md`. It lists the imported kernel items, why the caller cannot pass the value in, and what rebuilds.

body:
**Stacked on #2112** (rest Adaptive, `mkinney:issue/2031-rest-adaptive`, head 71a7fee47). This PR's own change is its last commit (c234093ee); until #2112 merges the diff against main shows #2112's commits too. Merge #2112 first.

Tests only (no product code): three pins the M5 review of #2112 found missing.

- **Raster half of the entry proof** - `machining2d::adaptive::rest::tests::the_raster_half_of_the_entry_proof_refuses_on_its_own` (unit test, `crates/motion/src/machining2d/adaptive/rest/tests.rs`). It hands `Entries` a raster holding a 1 mm pillar that the polygon bound does not hold, then asks for a plunge whose rim would stand 0.2 mm inside the pillar: refused. A plunge clear of the pillar by more than the margin is still proved. Inside the planner the raster comes from the same polygon bound (grown), and the polygon half refuses everything the raster would, so no planner fixture can make the raster refuse on its own. The test therefore works on `Entries` directly.
  - Mutation-checked: removing `&& self.stock.air(p, p, self.footprint)` from `Entries::proved` turns it red, and so does `footprint: 0.0`.
- **Load ceiling on the default D/80 measuring grid** - `on_the_default_measuring_grid_the_load_stays_under_its_documented_ceiling` (`crates/motion/tests/rest_adaptive/main.rs`). Optimal x 1.2 (`LOAD_CEILING_D80` in `sim.rs`, with its readings documented), on the climb 3 mm corners and on the conventional 3.5 mm corners with 0.3 mm left.
- **Corner assertion on a fine grid (D/240)** - `on_a_fine_grid_the_corners_read_within_the_planning_margin`. A 26 x 22 pocket with 3.5 mm corners, cut conventionally with 0.3 mm left. On the measuring stock that is 1680 x 1440 cells, under the 4096-cell cap. It must read within the planner's own margin (optimal x 1.05), and every feed stays in the corners.
- `sim.rs`: `Sim::on_grid(region, cell)` and `assert_load_within(reading, slack)`. `assert_load_held` is now `assert_load_within(.., LOAD_SLACK)`.

title: refactor(log): library and UI diagnostics become tracing events
body:
## What changed

The last slice of #163, after PR #222 (app seams: save/open/post/generate/commands) and PR #969 (app library eprintln!s and the budget-refusal events). With this, no diagnostic in the library or UI crates bypasses the one `tracing` subscriber any more.

- **Library crates** (`camcraft-cl`, `-geometry`, `-motion`, `-sim`, `-tools`): every non-test `eprintln!` is now a `tracing` event - refusals and fallbacks at `warn` (refused move/builder axis or C angle; multi-axis moves held vertical or radial, a rotary start on the axis, a degenerate drive curve skipped; a non-finite sim path left out or move held still; the dual iso-surface falling back to marching tetrahedra; a missing starter tool catalog), the opt-in `CAMCRAFT_PROFILE_PROJECTION` profile lines at `info`. The text of each line is unchanged.
- **Standalone bins** (`camcraft-cl`, `-geometry`, `-motion`, `-sim`, `-tools`): each installs a stderr subscriber with the app's filter rule (`CAMCRAFT_LOG`, else `RUST_LOG`, else `info`), so the converted library warnings still reach their terminal. Their own `println!` reports and usage errors are the CLI's answer and stay as they are.
- **UI**: the `diag` seam (#31) now emits `tracing` events natively (target `camcraft_ui`, `warn`/`info`) instead of `eprintln!`/`println!`; wasm32 still goes to the browser console. The native window (`shell_window.rs`, `shell_window/frame.rs`), GPU bring-up (`gpu_init.rs`), Cmd+Q hook (`os_quit.rs`) and the headless proof (`shell.rs`) now speak through the seam, so the law test's allow-list shrinks to the seam and test-only code (`gpu.rs`'s test module, `headless_gpu.rs`'s `device_for_test`, whose "SKIPPED - NOT a pass" line must show in a test run with no subscriber).

title: feat(sim): add spun and extruded fixture profiles with DXF and STEP support
body:
Stacked on #2077 (merge #2077 first)

Fork synced at v0.21.0.

## What changed

- Added ASCII DXF annotation (`TEXT`/`MTEXT`) reading and an original ASCII DXF writer in `crates/geometry/src/dxf/`.
- Added DXF profile parsing, validation, solid meshing, and mesh-silhouette derivation in `crates/geometry/src/dxf_profile.rs`, `profile_mesh.rs`, and `profile_derive.rs`.
- Supported revolved spun half-profiles (`CENTRELINE`/`AXIS` around `+Z`, convertible with `#743` `SpunProfile`) and extruded closed 2D contours along `X`/`Y`/`Z` with positive depth.
- Preserved raw STEP bytes in ECS `StepSource`, `.camproj` (`EntityDto.step_source`), and `.camfixtures` (`FixtureEntry.step_source`), never converting imported STEP fixtures into profiles on import.
- Added undoable commands `InsertProfileFixture`, `SetFixtureProfile`, and `DeriveFixtureProfile`, plus five MCP tools in `crates/app/src/mcp/fixture_profile_tools.rs`.
- `DeriveFixtureProfile` and `derive_fixture_profile` derive a reference profile only from a STEP fixture. They refuse, by name, a DXF/profile fixture and an imported mesh fixture without a STEP source. Thus the profile that defines the steel stays the collision bound.
- Added the `"Add DXF / profile…"` dialog and per-row edit/derive/DXF-export controls in `crates/ui`, keeping `crates/ui/src/egui_app/fixture_menu.rs` untouched.
- Added decision record `docs/decisions/744-fixture-profiles.md`.

## Cause

Turning chucks, jaws, collets, vises, parallels, and step blocks lacked parametric 2D profile authoring, DXF import/export, and post-placement profile editing. Vendor STEP fixtures needed to keep their raw STEP geometry intact rather than being replaced by approximated profiles.

## Tests

Pins:
- `camcraft-geometry --test dxf_profile`: `spun_fixture_imports_from_dxf_centreline_plus_half_profile_and_roundtrips`, `extruded_fixture_reads_closed_profile_and_depth_from_annotation_or_arg`, `dxf_profile_malformed_inputs_give_named_errors_never_panic` (3 passed).

- `camcraft-app --test fixture_step_library`: `step_fixture_saves_to_library_as_step_and_reinserts_unchanged` (1 passed).
- `camcraft-app --test mcp_fixture_profile`: `mcp_fixture_profile_workflow_imports_edits_exports_and_keeps_step`, `mcp_derive_fixture_profile_refuses_generated_fixture_and_keeps_its_profile` (2 passed).
- `camcraft-app --test fixture_profile_collision`: `generated_fixture_refuses_reference_derivation_and_keeps_its_collision_bound`, `mesh_fixture_without_step_source_refuses_reference_derivation`, plus the 4 earlier collision tests (6 passed).
- `camcraft-ui --lib egui_app::fixture_profile_tests`: `fixtures_page_button_opens_profile_dialog_and_inserts_dxf_fixtures`, `refused_profile_or_bad_dxf_is_named_in_dialog`, `editing_placed_profile_row_regenerates_mesh_and_exports_dxf`, `step_fixture_keeps_raw_step_and_allows_reference_derive_only` (4 passed inside 852 lib tests).

Mutation checks:
- Weakened `dxf_profile::resolve_depth` positive-depth guard (`> 0.0`): `dxf_profile_malformed_inputs_give_named_errors_never_panic` failed red, restored and passed green.
- Disabled `SetFixtureProfile::new` STEP-source guard in `profile_fixture.rs`: `mcp_fixture_profile_workflow_imports_edits_exports_and_keeps_step` failed red, restored and passed green.
- Cleared `ImportModel::apply` `step_source::set` write in `import_model.rs`: `step_fixture_saves_to_library_as_step_and_reinserts_unchanged` failed red, restored and passed green.
- Disabled the STEP-source guard in `target_fixture` (`profile_fixture.rs`): both new `fixture_profile_collision` tests and `mcp_derive_fixture_profile_refuses_generated_fixture_and_keeps_its_profile` failed red, restored and passed green.

none (`git diff --stat upstream/main -- "*.nc" "*.cl"` is empty).

title: feat(tools): convert STEP bodies to DXF half-profiles and import/export DXF
body:
## What changed

- Added a clean-room ASCII DXF writer in `crates/geometry/src/dxf/writer.rs` (`dxf::write`, `dxf::write_bytes`, `Unit::code`) emitting `HEADER` (`$INSUNITS`), `TABLES` (`LAYER`), and `ENTITIES` (`LINE`, `ARC`, `CIRCLE`).
- Added conservative stepped-band reduction in `crates/tools/src/spun_envelope.rs` (`SpunProfile::conservative_from_bands`) merging adjacent `HolderBand`s strictly upward (`max(r)`) down to at most 31 bands (`<= 64` points) and `MIN_SEGMENT`.
- Added STEP and `ToolBody` <-> ASCII DXF half-profile conversion and DXF import in `crates/app/src/tool_profile_dxf.rs` and `crates/app/src/tool_profile_dxf_import.rs` with explicit `CENTRELINE` and `PROFILE` layers.
- Added undoable `SetToolBody` constructors (`from_dxf_bytes`, `from_dxf`, `from_step_profile`, `from_placed_profile`, `profile_dxf`) in `crates/app/src/commands/tool_body_dxf.rs` over `tool_body::build_spun`.
- Registered MCP tools `import_tool_holder_dxf`, `export_tool_holder_dxf`, and `convert_tool_step_to_profile` in `crates/app/src/mcp/holder_dxf_tools.rs`.
- Added conservative-envelope and half-profile-only notices, `Import DXF…`, `Export DXF…`, `Import STEP…`, and Body tab `Convert to profile` in `crates/ui/src/state_tool_profile.rs`, `tool_profile_page.rs`, and `tool_body_page.rs`.
- Recorded architectural trade-offs in `docs/decisions/743-step-dxf-half-profile.md`.

## Cause

- Direct conversion from `HolderProfile::envelope` to `SpunProfile` failed above 31 stepped bands because `2 * 32 + 2 = 66` exceeds `MAX_POINTS` (`64`).
- CamCraft lacked an ASCII DXF writer and could not export or re-import tool holder half-profiles with an explicit centreline or enforce ISO 13399 CSYS alignment on STEP-to-profile conversion.

## Tests

- Pins:
  - `camcraft-geometry::dxf_writer`: `write_and_parse_round_trip_lines_arcs_circles_layers_and_units`, `writer_refuses_invalid_inputs_by_name` (2 passed).

  - `camcraft-app::tool_dxf_profile_mcp`: `mcp_holder_dxf_and_step_profile_tools_list_round_trip_undo_and_refuse` (1 passed).
  - `camcraft-ui::egui_app::tests::tool_profile` (9 passed, adding `profile_tab_states_conservative_envelope_and_half_profile_rules_and_dxf_workflow` and `body_tab_convert_to_profile_refuses_unaligned_step_and_converts_iso_aligned_step`).
- Mutations (each tested red after weakening the guard and green after restore):
  - `spun_envelope::join` `max(r)` -> `min(r)`: failed `thirty_two_distinct_bands_reduce_conservatively_to_spun_profile`; restored green.
  - `dxf::writer` zero-length `LINE` guard bypassed: failed `writer_refuses_invalid_inputs_by_name`; restored green.
  - `tool_profile_dxf_import` centreline-crossing guard bypassed: failed `dxf_half_profile_error_refusals_never_panic_and_name_reasons`; restored green.
  - `step_to_spun_profile` ISO 13399 requirement replaced with `+Z` fallback: failed `step_conversion_refuses_missing_or_ambiguous_axis_by_name`; restored green.
  - `convert_body_draft_to_profile` clear-axis check bypassed: failed `body_tab_convert_to_profile_refuses_unaligned_step_and_converts_iso_aligned_step`; restored green.
- Gate:
  - `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main` expanded to the `batch` tier (`crates/geometry/src/dxf/mod.rs` is a shared crate) and passed all 10 steps in 39.8 min with 0 failures (`geometry`, `kernel`, `cl`, `tools`, `post`, `sim`, `motion`, `app`, `ui`, `clippy -D warnings`).

## Not exercised

title: feat(tools)!: a tool's library holder is a reference to the entry
body:
Stacked on #2054 (branch `mkinney:issue/2018-weldon-per-taper`, with `main` merged in for #2029). Merge #2054 first; this diff then shows only the #2016 commits. Fork synced from upstream `main` at c86d6db35.

## What changed

A tool that sits in a built-in library holder stores a reference to the entry, not a drawn copy of its outline.

- `camcraft_tools::holder_library::HolderRef {entry, gauge_len, projection}` (new, `crates/tools/src/holder_library_ref.rs`), carried on `ToolBody::library`.
- `tool_body::build_library` is the one place a reference becomes a shape. `SetToolBody::library`, `AddTool` (stated and machine-default holder), the project loader and the `.camtools` reader call it. `tool_body::judged`, `stack`, `digest`, the simulation and the preview read the body it returns, as before. The #828 floor for a machine-default holder is unchanged.
- Files: the tool key `holder: {entry, gauge_len, projection}` (plus `machine_default: true` when assumed) is written in place of `body`. Project v62 (the unreleased step the issue names); a `.camtools` file says version 2 when a tool names a library holder.
- Migration: an older file is not rewritten. A drawn copy of a library holder stays a custom drawn profile with the same outline, and a `holder_d`/`holder_len` cylinder stays the tool's own numbers.
- Refusals by tool name: an entry the library does not hold, a grouped pick ("BT40 Weldon"), lengths the entry cannot take, a holder that reaches into the flutes, an unknown key in the reference, `holder` beside `body`. No other holder is put in its place.
- MCP: `set_tool_holder` with `library` writes the reference; the reply and `get_job` show it as `holder.library`. `add_tool` refuses a `holder` reference inside `definition`; `edit_tool` refuses a `holder` patch. Skill rows updated.
- UI: with a referenced holder the tool settings show the holder diameter and length the laws read as text, not as two fields. The Profile tab names the entry and the picker shows it. The unchanged outline applied again keeps the reference; one edited point makes the holder a custom profile (one undo step).

Decisions: `docs/decisions/2016-holder-reference.md`.

## How tested

`cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main` green on the final head (tools, app and ui suites), and `cargo clippy -p camcraft-tools -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -- -D warnings` clean. macOS (m5).

Pinning tests:

- `crates/app/tests/holder_reference.rs`
  - `every_entry_reads_the_same_bands_by_reference_as_its_old_copy`: for every library entry, at the default and at other lengths, picked and assumed: the judged tool, envelope, band stack, stamp term and facets equal those of the drawn copy an older build stored, also after a save and load.
  - `an_older_project_loads_as_custom_holders_with_the_same_collision_result`: a v61 project with a drawn copy and a plain holder cylinder loads with the same reads, operation status and warnings (the BT30 flange strikes the fixture wall, hit for hit).
  - `an_older_tool_library_loads_as_custom_holders_and_a_new_one_round_trips_the_reference`
  - `an_unknown_entry_refuses_the_file_by_name_and_never_lands_another_holder` (project and `.camtools`)
  - `a_library_holder_is_the_reference_in_the_document_and_the_file`
  - `the_unchanged_outline_keeps_the_reference_and_an_edited_point_makes_it_custom`
  - `mcp_set_tool_holder_writes_the_reference`
- `crates/tools/src/holder_library_ref.rs` unit tests.
- `crates/ui/src/egui_app/tests/tool_holder_reference.rs`: `a_library_holder_sizes_the_holder_fields_until_its_outline_is_edited`, `the_profile_tab_names_the_entry_and_the_picker_shows_it`.

## Not exercised

- Windows and Linux. The release tier and the pixel-snapshot lanes (no snapshot PNG changed).
- No real v0.21.0 file was read: the older file in the tests is this build's file rewritten to the older form (`body` with the drawn copy, version 61 / 1).
- The app was not driven by hand.

First slice of #1468. Fork synced from `upstream/main` at 31f8d03d7 (branch cut from it, not from a tag). Not stacked: no open PR changes these files except the camcraft-mcp skill (#1738, #1817, #2037 edit other rows).

## What changed

- **Dialog: "Fit to the stock" for a lathe chuck.** "Add accessory…" shows a **Fit to the stock** checkbox for the 3-jaw, 4-jaw and collet chuck. Ticked, Place queues `InsertAccessory` with the existing `OnStock` placement; the grip diameter (or collet bore) is shown as "(set by the fit)" and disabled, and the pose rows give way to a line that says what the fit does. The box opens ticked when the setup's stock reads as round.
- **Inside grip** (`JawChuck::grip`, `outside` | `inside`). An inside jaw runs inward from the grip diameter; its gripping face is the arc of the bore it opens into, drawn circumscribed (flats on the grip circle, steps of at most 1/256 turn), so the drawn steel is never less than the jaw.
- **Stepped jaws** (`step_height`, `step_depth`; both 0 for plain jaws). Below the step height the jaw reaches the step depth past the gripping face, under the work. A stock fit seats the stock on the step: the chuck's face goes the step height below the stock's underside.
- **Refusals by name** (all in `camcraft_sim::chuck::jaw::check`): a step figure that is not finite, negative or over 5000 mm; one step figure without the other; a step as tall as its jaw; a step or an inside jaw that reaches the axis; steps or inside jaws that would meet each other; an inside jaw wider than its bore, shorter than its own arc, or past the body. A stock fit with an inside grip is refused ("an inside grip opens into the work's bore, which the stock's box does not give"); the dialog unticks and disables the box for an inside grip and says why.
- **MCP:** `add_accessory` and `set_accessory` take `grip`; the `dimensions` object takes `step_height` and `step_depth`; the result's `accessory` shows `grip` for a jaw chuck. The camcraft-mcp skill row now lists the three chuck kinds, `fit_to_stock`, `grip` and the step figures.

- Guide: `site/content/guide/set-up/workholding.md` describes the chuck rows. Decision record: `docs/decisions/1468-chuck-options.md`.

The jaw geometry lives in `crates/sim/src/chuck/jaw.rs` (new, with its provenance line); `chuck.rs` keeps the body, the collet and the round-stock read. No new crate dependency.

title: fix(post): honor or refuse G83 dwell per control
body:
Stacked on #1821 (merge #1821 first)

## What changed

Fanuc, Doosan DNM and Mazak refuse a positive G83 dwell by name.
Zero-dwell G83 remains available.
Haas keeps integer milliseconds and includes dwell in its G83 cycle signature.
Haas writes P0 to clear a previous dwell.

## Cause

The posts wrote P without checking G83 support for each control.
Haas omitted dwell from its cycle signature and omitted zero P.
That could reuse an earlier dwell.
Fanuc's standard milling G83 format has no P.
Mazak's detailed format and summary disagree, so this post refuses dwell conservatively.
The decision record links the public control manuals and explains these limits.

title: fix(2d): clear Zigzag rest boundaries without wall cusps
body:
Stacked on #1817 (merge #1817 first)

## What changed

2D rest machining now accepts Zigzag. It cuts rows, then closes each rest boundary to clear wall cusps.

Rows use an inset of `min(0.01 mm, stepover / 4)`. This prevents numeric boundary crossings without removing interior rows from small pockets.

The existing plain-pocket row algorithm moves unchanged to `pocket_zigzag.rs`. `pocket.rs` stays at 398 lines. No dependency is added.

The MCP skill now describes Zigzag support. Adaptive still has its named refusal. The entered previous tool remains an explicit trust assumption.

The remaining #1490 work has separate issues: Adaptive #2031, entry from cleared space #2032, and previous-operation stock #2033.

## Cause

Rows alone leave cusps at the rest boundary. A closing pass clears them. Rows that touch the boundary can cross it through numeric rounding.

A fixed 0.01 mm inset removes all rows from a tiny pocket. The stepover cap preserves those rows.

The geometry follows this project's existing scan and offset routines. See Held's [Zigzag Pocket Machining](https://www.cosy.sbg.ac.at/~held/projects/pocket_zig/pocket.html) and [pocket geometry monograph](https://link.springer.com/book/10.1007/3-540-54103-9). [Yao, Gupta and Nau](https://www.cs.umd.edu/~nau/papers/yao2003algorithms.pdf) provide the cutter-coverage context. The inset and closing-pass choices are ours.

## Tests

- `zigzag_rest_covers_corner_residue_without_gouges_or_unsafe_rapids`: red at the original refusal. Green after the fix. Covers both directions and 1.5/4 mm steps.
- `tiny_rest_pocket_keeps_interior_rows_when_previous_tool_fits_nowhere`: red with the fixed inset. Green with the stepover cap.
- Expected-change tests now accept Zigzag at the motion and operation parameter doors.
- Closing-pass mutation: red coverage; restored green. The first fixture left 287 measured residue points uncut.
- Zero-inset mutation: red verifier, with six crossings; restored green.
- Fixed-inset mutation: red tiny-pocket center coverage; restored green.
- Old `upstream/main` pocket code: red; restored green.
- Old `base-1817` rest strategy: red refusal; restored green. The parent baseline supplies the export absent from `upstream/main`.

The requested `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main` passed all three steps in 34.4 minutes before the inset cap.

After the cap, `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main --only motion` passed its affected motion step in 663 seconds.

`cargo clippy -p camcraft-motion -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -- -D warnings` passed on the final code.

## Goldens moved

None from #1490. The diff against `base-1817` changes no `.nc` or `.cl` file.

The two-dot diff against `upstream/main` lists 147 files. All were checked against the merge base and parent.
Of these, 146 exactly reverse upstream changes absent from the older parent branch. The other is #1817's unchanged `pocket_rest_corners.cl` addition.

## Not exercised

No real machine was used. This change does not implement new Adaptive paths, cleared-space entry, or previous-operation stock input.
Those features require separate depth and cutter-clearance proofs in #2031, #2032, and #2033.

## Overlaps

- #1817 changes `rest_pocket`, `rest_strategy`, and the expected-refusal tests. This branch stacks on its head.
- #2013 and #1954 touch the same file, different module declarations in `machining2d/mod.rs`; whichever merges second refreshes.
- #1738 touches the same file, a different section of the MCP skill; whichever merges second refreshes.

Decision record: `docs/decisions/1490-rest-strategies.md`.

Effort: max

title: fix(fidelity): a stock copy of an incomplete model keeps naming its hole
body:
A stock copied from an incomplete model (#1610) now keeps naming that model's hole after the model is deleted. Before this change, its refusal at the post fell back to "saved before CamCraft recorded mesh fidelity (project v58 or older)". The post still refused it; only the reason given was wrong.

Fixes #1700

## What changed

The copy's refusal read the hole from the source model by name (`mesh_open::unknown_note`), so once the source was gone the lookup found nothing. Now the copy carries the hole itself (`schema::MeshOpen`), beside the fidelity-unknown sentinel it already carried (#1056):

- **Where the hole is copied:** every place that lands the sentinel on a copy now lands the hole with it:
  - `SetStock` and its undo
  - a setup clone (`CreateSetup` with a datum)
  - an undone `DeleteSetup`
  - `UpdateModel`'s refresh of the copies, and its undo
  - the project loader
- **Where the refusal reads it:** `model_fidelity::op_problem` reads the hole off the entity that carries the sentinel. Two small helpers: `mesh_open::hole_behind` (the twin of `model_fidelity::chord_behind`) and `mesh_open::note_for`.
- **Project file:** the saver already wrote `mesh_open` for any entity that has one. The loader now also accepts it on a `FromModel` stock marked `fidelity_unknown`, and a hole without the mark stays corrupt. There is no version bump: #1610's check (a hole on anything but a model is corrupt) has not shipped in a cut yet, so no released reader refuses these files.

The decisions are recorded in `docs/decisions/1700-stock-copy-hole.md`.

## How tested

- **New:** `crates/app/tests/stock_copy_hole.rs` (6 tests). A copy carries the hole, and its refusal names the source and the hole:
  - after the source is deleted, and across undo and redo of that delete;
  - after save, load, and a second save that matches byte for byte;
  - through a setup clone and an undone setup delete;
  - through a whole re-import of the source (which clears it) and that re-import's undo;
  - through `SetStock`'s undo.

  The file also checks that a stock with a hole and no mark fails to load as corrupt.
- **Without the fix,** the two "source deleted" tests fail: the refusal reads "saved before CamCraft recorded …".
- **Existing tests:** the `import_step_open_shell` tests from #1610 still pass. Its corrupt-file message check passes too, because the new message keeps the old wording as a prefix.
- **Gate:** `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main` is green (112 app suites), and `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app --tests -- -D warnings` is clean.

Branched from upstream/main after #1699 merged, not from a cut tag: the code this fixes is not in v0.20.0.

title: fix(ui): keep the near plane and the ortho eye consistent with the zoom
body:
### Summary

A viewport fix for the way the camera eats the model from the inside.

Two ways the camera clipped the model while zooming:

- **Perspective:** the near plane was a fixed 0.1 mm from the eye, so at close zoom the geometry right in front of the near plane clipped instead of rendering — zooming in went through the model. The near plane now rides `dist` (0.1 % of the view depth, clamped to 1e-5 min and 0.1 max).
- **Orthographic:** `dist` moved the eye, so zooming dollied the eye into the model and clipped through its faces from inside. The eye now sits at a fixed nominal distance (100 mm) behind the target, and `dist` is only a zoom factor for the view box's half-height — the way it was always meant to work. The near plane now reaches far behind the eye plane: `-((dist * 20.0).max(1000.0) - ORTHO_EYE_DIST)`.

Changelog: UI — the perspective near plane moves with the dolly distance and the orthographic camera's near plane no longer clips through geometry while zooming.

The tests pin the new ortho depth formula and a point in front of the eye plane (`dist = 300`, 150 mm back from the target), asserting it stays inside the clip volume.

### Verification

`cargo test -p camcraft-ui --lib` — 803 passed. `cargo clippy -p camcraft-ui --all-targets` — clean. No posted G-code, collision check, stock simulation math or geometry changed.

No issue covers this viewport bug yet — a maintainer will file one.

title: feat(turning): in-pass chip-break dips inside a continuous G32 chain
body:
The stack parents #517 (#417) and #518 (#418) are merged. The diff now holds only the #419 work.

## Merge-time refresh (maintainer's session, head 39632f647)
The maintainer's session took this PR over for a merge-time refresh. It merged `origin/main` (62e1d36a6) into the branch. It did not rebase or force-push.

Hand-resolved hunks (keep both sides):
- `assets/posts/fanuc-lathe.cps`, `threadHalfTurn`: the PR's dip chain is kept. Main changed the lead word from `fr()` to `fl()` (#902: an inch lead has six decimals). Both G32 blocks of the chain (the plain block and the dip block `G32 X Z F`) now use `fl()`. The three refusals of the chain (no open chain, steeper than 45 degrees, deeper than the pass) are kept.
- `assets/posts/fanuc-lathe.cps`, manifest: `continuousThreading = true` with its citation, and main's `workOffsetIndex`, `workOffsetMax`, `explainWords`, `explainTool`, `programUnits`, `explains`, `commentMax`, `explainBlockMax`.
- `assets/posts/fanuc-lathe.cps`, G76 header comment: the PR's chip-break dips clause and main's `g76Allowance` paragraph (#517). `g76Why` keeps the two refusals: `RepeatEachDepth` (#518) and `ChipBreakDips`.
- `assets/posts/AGENTS.md`: main's manifest list with `continuousThreading` added ("the last nine").
- `crates/post/src/post/engine.rs`: the `ChipBreakDips` refusal and main's `MillSpindle` reverse refusal (#988).
- `crates/post/src/post/js.rs`: the `continuous_threading` and `mill_spindle_reverse` fields.

No refusal of #517, #518 or main is lost. The Tormach lathe post does not declare `continuousThreading`, so the engine refuses dips on it by name. Its G76 `RepeatEachDepth` refusal (#518) is unchanged. `git diff origin/main --stat` lists only the 26 files of this PR.

Readings after the refresh (`cargo test -j 6 -p <crate> --test <binary>`, one binary at a time):
- camcraft-motion: `turning_thread_dips` 9/9, `turning_thread_cycle` 3/3, `turning_thread_infeed` 10/10, lib 366 passed (5 ignored).
- camcraft-post: `inverted_post` 16/16, `recorded_streams` 12/12, lib 54/54.
- camcraft-cl: lib 41/41.
- camcraft-app: `lathe_post_thread_dips` 6/6 (golden `thread_g32_dips.nc` unchanged), `lathe_post_g76` 8/8, `lathe_post_g76_schedule` 7/7, `lathe_post_tormach_thread` 8/8, `lathe_post_css` 10/10, `turning_thread` 10/10, `turning_thread_infeed` 5/5, `lathe_thread_travel` 2/2, `conformance` 7/7, `coarse_laws` 6/6, `lathe_field_tools` 2/2, `project_roundtrip` 73/73.
- camcraft-ui: lib filter `thread` 6/6.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-post -p camcraft-cl -p camcraft-motion -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.

Not exercised by the refresh: an inch program with dips (the `fl()` lead word under G20 has no golden), and a run on a controller or a simulator.

MCP: the dips ride the generic `edit_operation` tool through the project params JSON (`ThreadInfeedDto.dips`). No new MCP tool is necessary.

Screenshots: before and after screenshots on the refreshed head are in the section "Screenshots (Passes tab)" below.

Note: `crates/post/src/post/engine.rs` (600 lines) and `js.rs` (529 lines) were already more than 400 lines on main. This PR adds 4 and 17 lines to them.

## The citation gate (the issue's precondition)
Before any code, the issue required a primary-source citation that chained Fanuc G32 blocks keep spindle synchronization. Found in *FANUC Series 0i-TD/0i Mate-TD USER'S MANUAL (For Lathe System)*, B-64304EN-1/01, Part II:
- **§3.4 "Continuous Threading", p.34:** consecutive threading blocks keep "the synchronism with the spindle" at "the joint between blocks wherever possible", so the lead and shape can change midway.
- **§3.2 "Constant Lead Threading (G32)", WARNING 6, p.32:** a threading block that follows a threading block starts "without waiting for detection of the one-spindle-rotation signal".
- **§3.2, pp.29-31:** G32 cuts tapers (`G32 X41.0 Z29.0 F3.5`). Up to 45° the lead F is taken along Z.

The manual was read from a public third-party mirror of Fanuc's PDF (https://www.slideshare.net/slideshow/fanuc-0itd-users-manualpdf/259106078), for behaviour only. The Haas G32 reference (cited in #363) agrees. **LinuxCNC G33 stays unconfirmed:** its docs don't say whether a chained G33 waits for the index again, so no LinuxCNC post may declare the capability.

## What changed
- **Parameters.** The infeed plan gains `ThreadInfeed.dips` with interval, height and length. An interval of 0 means off, which is the default.
- **Shape of a dip.** A dip is a radial lift on **roughing passes only**. Each ramp stays under 45°, keeping the lead on Z.
  - **Never placed in:** the first or last lead, or the finishing, spring or #418 repeat passes.
  - **Height:** no more than every dipped pass's depth of cut.
- **New CL segment.** A dip is a variable-radius XY half-turn: the axial travel is still exactly half a lead, but the end radius differs from the start.
- **Marking.** The thread record carries `chip_break_dips`: `DIP 1` in the stream, `ChipBreakDips` as a post property, and a project cache key only when set. The section carries `PARAM ChipBreakDips`. If dips are on but the record can't be attached, the kernel refuses, so a dip is never laid unmarked.
- **Post capability flag.** The engine refuses dips by name for any script without `continuousThreading = true`. Only `fanuc-lathe.cps` declares it, with the citation in its header.
  - It writes each dip segment as `G32 X Z F`.
  - It refuses by name a segment that doesn't continue a G32 chain, is steeper than 45°, or goes deeper than its plunge.
  - **G76 refuses dips by name.**
- **Verdict.** `thread_warnings` checks every chain for phase (equal axial advance per half-turn), depth, slope and placement. Any breach is a Gouge, which blocks the post.
- **UI.** Three rows on the Passes tab.
- **Defaults are byte-identical.** With dips off there is no stamp byte, project key, stream word or PARAM.
- `docs/decisions/419-thread-dips.md`

## How tested
- **New motion `turning_thread_dips`** (8 tests):
  - dips off lay the plain path bit for bit;
  - a dip is never deeper than its pass;
  - the phase is unchanged across the chain;
  - placement and slope rules hold;
  - a repeated depth cuts whole;
  - the verdict is silent on laid dips;
  - the verdict convicts each broken law (first/last lead, finishing pass, deeper, phase shift, steep). Temporarily disabling the laws made this test fail.
  - refusals by name.
- **New app `lathe_post_thread_dips`** (6 tests):
  - the golden `thread_g32_dips.nc`;
  - the posted chain keeps the plain thread's Z words and lead;
  - G76 refuses;
  - a post without `continuousThreading` refuses;
  - the lathe script refuses a bent dip;
  - dips ride the command, the stream and the project file.
- **Existing suites green:** the turning thread, infeed and G76 suites, `inverted_post`, `lathe_post*`, `project_roundtrip`, `conformance`, and all cl and post tests. No existing golden changed.
- `clippy -D warnings --all-targets` on motion, post, cl, app and ui is clean.

## Not exercised (draft)
- **Machine check:** a run on a lathe simulator or machine.
- **GUI check:** the Passes-tab rows. The #416 test kit covers the neighbouring rows.

Fixes #419
